subject: math
title: Time: Units of Time, Clocks, a.m. and p.m., Calendars and Elapsed Time
seo_title: Grade 3 Time Worksheets: Clocks, Calendars and Elapsed Time (Free, BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on time for the BC curriculum: units of time from seconds to years, reading analog clocks to the 5 minutes and to the minute, a.m. and p.m., calendars, and elapsed time word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: 1 hour = 60 minutes, not 100. Short hand: the hour. Long hand: count by 5s, then by 1s.
key_sub: 1 minute = 60 seconds, 1 day = 24 hours, 1 week = 7 days, 1 year = 12 months. If the short hand has not reached a number yet, it is still the hour before. On a calendar, count the jumps, not the first day.
body_html:
Units of time

We measure time with seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months and years. Time does not count in tens or hundreds. Learn these facts:

UnitIs the same as
1 minute60 seconds
1 hour60 minutes
1 day24 hours
1 week7 days
1 year12 months, about 52 weeks, 365 days

Short things, like a sneeze, take seconds. A school day takes hours. Summer holidays take months.

Read an analog clock

The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes. Each number is 5 minutes for the long hand, so count by 5s. Between two numbers there are 5 small marks, one for each minute.

DigitalWe say
4:15quarter past 4
4:30half past 4
4:45quarter to 5
4:5010 to 5

a.m. and p.m.

a.m. is from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening).

a.m. or p.m.?

Ava eats breakfast at 25 to 8. Write the time.

25 to 8 is 35 minutes past 7. Breakfast is in the morning, so it is a.m.

Answer: 7:35 a.m.

Read a calendar

Each row of a calendar is 1 week. Look up a column to find the day of the week. To count days, count the jumps. Do not count the first day.

Days in a month

How many days are in November?

April, June, September and November have 30 days. February has 28 (29 in a leap year). The rest have 31.

Answer: 30 days

Elapsed time: how long?

An hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Jump to the next o’clock first, then on to the end time.

Find the end time

A ferry leaves at 9:20 a.m. The trip takes 1 hour 35 minutes. When does it arrive?

Add 1 hour: 10:20 a.m. Add 35 minutes: 20 + 35 = 55.

Answer: 10:55 a.m.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Swapping the hands: reading 8:35 as 7:40The short hand is the hour. The long hand is the minutes
Short hand just before 9 read as 9:35The short hand has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is still 8: 8:35
Long hand on 4 read as 4 minutesEach number is 5 minutes: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes
10:50 to 11:20 worked out as 1120 − 1050 = 70 minutesAn hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Count on: 10 + 20 = 30 minutes
Counting the first day: May 4 to May 6 is 3 daysCount the jumps: 6 − 4 = 2 days
Breakfast at 7:30 p.m.Morning times are a.m.: 7:30 a.m.

faq.q: What do Grade 3 students learn about time in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 3 math curriculum lists time concepts under Geometry and measurement. Students learn units of time from seconds to years, read clocks, use a.m. and p.m., read calendars and work out how long events last.

faq.q: How many days are in each month?
faq.a: April, June, September and November have 30 days. February has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year. All the other months have 31 days.

faq.q: What is the difference between a.m. and p.m.?
faq.a: a.m. times are from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. times are from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening), so school starts at an a.m. time and dinner is at a p.m. time.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn to tell time?
faq.a: Keep an analog clock and a wall calendar at home. Ask the time at everyday moments like breakfast and bedtime, count the days to a birthday together, and practise counting by 5s around the clock.

sets.title: Units of time: seconds to years

items.q: How many seconds are in 1 minute?
items.e: There are 60 seconds in 1 minute. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds.)

items.q: How many minutes are in 1 hour?
items.e: There are 60 minutes in 1 hour. The long hand goes once around the clock. (Not 100: an hour is not like a hundred.)

items.q: How many hours are in 1 day?
items.e: The short hand goes around the clock 2 times in a day: 12 + 12 = 24 hours. (12 is only half a day.)

items.q: How many days are in 1 week?
items.e: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday: 7 days. (5 is only the school days.)

items.q: How many months are in 1 year?
items.e: January to December is 12 months. (52 is the number of weeks in a year.)

items.q: Which unit is best to measure how long a sneeze takes?
items.e: A sneeze is over very fast, so we use seconds.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure how long it takes to brush your teeth?
items.e: Brushing your teeth takes a few minutes, so we use minutes.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure how long a school day is?
items.e: A school day is from the morning to the afternoon, so we use hours.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure how long summer holidays in BC (July and August) are?
items.e: July and August are 2 whole months, so we use months.

items.q: Put these in order from shortest to longest: hour, second, day, minute
items.e: A second is very short. 60 seconds make a minute, 60 minutes make an hour, and 24 hours make a day. So the order is second, minute, hour, day.

items.q: Put these in order from shortest to longest: year, day, month, week
items.e: 7 days make a week. About 4 weeks make a month. 12 months make a year. So the order is day, week, month, year.

items.q: About how many weeks are in 1 year?
items.e: A year has 365 days. 52 weeks × 7 days = 364 days, so a year is about 52 weeks. (12 is the months and 365 is the days.)

items.q: 2 hours = ? minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 2 hours = 60 + 60 = 120 minutes. (Not 200: an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: 3 weeks = ? days
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 3 weeks = 7 + 7 + 7 = 21 days. (30 counts a week as 10 days.)

items.q: 2 days = ? hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. 2 days = 24 + 24 = 48 hours. (24 counts a day as 12 hours. 120 uses 60, but that is the minutes in an hour.)

items.q: 1 hour 15 minutes = ? minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 60 + 15 = 75 minutes. (115 counts an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: Which is the same as 90 minutes?
items.e: 60 minutes make 1 hour. 90 − 60 = 30 minutes left. So 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes. (1 hour 10 minutes would be 70 minutes.)

items.q: Which is longer: 100 minutes or 2 hours?
items.e: 2 hours = 60 + 60 = 120 minutes. 120 minutes is more than 100 minutes, so 2 hours is longer. (An hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Mei’s Spring Break is 2 weeks long. How many days is that?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 2 weeks = 7 + 7 = 14 days. (20 counts a week as 10 days.)

items.q: Simran’s baby cousin is 18 months old. How old is that in years and months?
items.e: 12 months make 1 year. 18 − 12 = 6 months left. So 18 months = 1 year 6 months. (1 year 8 months counts a year as 10 months.)

sets.title: Analog clocks to the 5 minutes and to the minute

items.e: The short hour hand points to 3. The long minute hand points to 12, so it is exactly on the hour. So the time is 3:00. (Not 12:15: that swaps the hands. Not 3:12: when the long hand points to 12, it is 0 minutes.)

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand points to 6. Count by 5s: 6 × 5 = 30 minutes. So the time is 8:30. (Not 9:30: the hour hand is before 9, so it is not 9 o’clock yet. Not 6:40: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 2 and 3. It has not reached 3 yet, so the hour is 2. The long minute hand points to 1. Count by 5s: 1 × 5 = 5 minutes. So the time is 2:05. (Not 2:01: each number is 5 minutes, so 1 means 1 × 5 = 5. Not 1:10: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1. It has not reached 1 yet, so the hour is 12. The long minute hand points to 3. Count by 5s: 3 × 5 = 15 minutes. 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour. The long hand is on the right side, so we say past. It is quarter past 12.

The short hour hand is between 10 and 11. It has not reached 11 yet, so the hour is 10. The long minute hand points to 4. Count by 5s: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes. So the time is 10:20. (Not 10:04: each number is 5 minutes, so 4 means 4 × 5 = 20. Not 4:50: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 2 and 3. It has not reached 3 yet, so the hour is 2. The long minute hand points to 8. Count by 5s: 8 × 5 = 40 minutes. So the time is 2:40. (Not 3:40: the hour hand is before 3, so it is not 3 o’clock yet. Not 8:10: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8. It has not reached 8 yet, so the hour is 7. The long minute hand points to 9. Count by 5s: 9 × 5 = 45 minutes. 45 minutes past 7 is 15 minutes before 8 o’clock. The long hand is on the left side, so we say to the next hour: quarter to 8.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand points to 5. Count by 5s: 5 × 5 = 25 minutes. So the time is 8:25. (Not 8:05: each number is 5 minutes, so 5 means 5 × 5 = 25. Not 5:40: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand points to 7. Count by 5s: 7 × 5 = 35 minutes. So the time is 8:35. (Not 9:35: the hour hand is before 9, so it is not 9 o’clock yet. Not 7:40: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 5 and 6. It has not reached 6 yet, so the hour is 5. The long minute hand points to 10. Count by 5s: 10 × 5 = 50 minutes. So the time is 5:50. (Not 6:50: the hour hand is before 6, so it is not 6 o’clock yet. Not 10:25: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 1. Count by 5s to 5, then by 1s: 7 minutes. So the time is 11:07. (Not 11:05: count the small marks after the 1 too.)

The short hour hand is between 9 and 10. It has not reached 10 yet, so the hour is 9. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 5. Count by 5s to 25, then by 1s: 29 minutes. So the time is 9:29. (Not 9:25: count the small marks after the 5 too.)

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2. It has not reached 2 yet, so the hour is 1. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 8. Count by 5s to 40, then by 1s: 44 minutes. So the time is 1:44. (Not 2:44: the hour hand has not reached 2 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 3 and 4. It has not reached 4 yet, so the hour is 3. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 11. Count by 5s to 55, then by 1s: 59 minutes. So the time is 3:59. (Not 4:59: the hour hand has not reached 4 yet.)

At 5:38 the long hand is 3 small marks past the 7 (count by 5s to 35, then by 1s to 38), and the short hand is between 5 and 6. That is clock D. (Clock A shows 6:38; clock B shows 5:22; clock C shows 5:07.)

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 3. Count by 5s to 15, then by 1s: 16 minutes. So the time is 11:16. (Not 11:15: count the small marks after the 3 too.)

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2. It has not reached 2 yet, so the hour is 1. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 6. Count by 5s to 30, then by 1s: 32 minutes. So the time is 1:32. (Not 2:32: the hour hand has not reached 2 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8. It has not reached 8 yet, so the hour is 7. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 10. Count by 5s to 50, then by 1s: 53 minutes. So the time is 7:53. (Not 8:53: the hour hand has not reached 8 yet.)

At 8:13 the long hand is 3 small marks past the 2 (count by 5s to 10, then by 1s to 13), and the short hand is between 8 and 9. That is clock A. (Clock B shows 9:13; clock C shows 8:47; clock D shows 8:02.)

The short hour hand is between 2 and 3. It has not reached 3 yet, so the hour is 2. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 9. Count by 5s to 45, then by 1s: 48 minutes. So the time is 2:48. (Not 3:48: the hour hand has not reached 3 yet.)

items.q: Which times are a.m. times?
items.e: a.m. times go from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. times go from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening).

items.q: What does noon mean?
c: the end of the school day
12 o’clock in the middle of the day
items.e: Noon is 12 o’clock in the middle of the day, when the morning ends. 12 o’clock at night is midnight.

items.q: Which time is in the afternoon?
items.e: The afternoon is after noon, so it is a p.m. time. 2:30 a.m. is in the middle of the night. So the answer is 2:30 p.m.

items.q: Which is a sensible time for school to start?
items.e: School starts in the morning, so it is an a.m. time. 3:40 a.m. is the middle of the night. So the answer is 8:40 a.m.

items.q: Arjun eats breakfast at 7:15 in the morning. Is that a.m. or p.m.?
c: a.m., because it is before noon
a.m., because it is after noon
p.m., because it is after noon
p.m., because it is before noon
items.e: Morning times are before noon. Times before noon are a.m. times. So breakfast is at 7:15 a.m.

items.q: Which is earlier in the same day: 11:50 a.m. or 1:10 p.m.?
items.e: a.m. times come before noon and p.m. times come after noon. So 11:50 a.m. is earlier, even though 11 is bigger than 1.

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8. It has not reached 8 yet, so the hour is 7. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 3. Count by 5s to 15, then by 1s: 17 minutes. It is in the morning, so it is a.m. So the time is 7:17 a.m. (Not 7:17 p.m.: that is in the afternoon or evening.)

items.q: Write quarter to 8 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “quarter to 8” means 15 minutes before 8 o’clock. 60 − 15 = 45, so it is 45 minutes past 7: 7:45. It is in the morning, so it is a.m.: 7:45 a.m.

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1. It has not reached 1 yet, so the hour is 12. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 1. Count by 5s to 5, then by 1s: 9 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 12:09 p.m. (Not 12:09 a.m.: that is in the middle of the night.)

items.q: Write 25 to 4 in the afternoon as a digital time.
items.e: “25 to 4” means 25 minutes before 4 o’clock. 60 − 25 = 35, so it is 35 minutes past 3: 3:35. It is in the afternoon, so it is p.m.: 3:35 p.m.

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 12: 3 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 6:03 p.m. (Not 6:03 a.m.: that is in the morning.)

items.q: Write 20 past 7 in the evening as a digital time.
items.e: “20 past 7” means 20 minutes after 7 o’clock: 7:20. It is in the evening, so it is p.m.: 7:20 p.m.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 2. Count by 5s to 10, then by 1s: 11 minutes. It is in the morning, so it is a.m. So the time is 8:11 a.m. (Not 8:11 p.m.: that is in the afternoon or evening.)

items.q: Write 10 to 11 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “10 to 11” means 10 minutes before 11 o’clock. 60 − 10 = 50, so it is 50 minutes past 10: 10:50. It is in the morning, so it is a.m.: 10:50 a.m.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 2. Count by 5s to 10, then by 1s: 13 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 8:13 p.m. (Not 8:13 a.m.: that is in the morning.)

The short hour hand is between 4 and 5. It has not reached 5 yet, so the hour is 4. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 5. Count by 5s to 25, then by 1s: 28 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 4:28 p.m. (Not 4:28 a.m.: that is in the middle of the night.)

items.q: How many hours is it from 9:00 a.m. to noon?
items.e: Count the jumps, not the numbers: 9:00 → 10:00 → 11:00 → 12:00 noon. That is 3 hours. (4 counts the numbers 9, 10, 11 and 12.)

items.q: How many hours is it from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.?
items.e: 11:00 a.m. → 12:00 noon is 1 hour. 12:00 noon → 2:00 p.m. is 2 hours. 1 + 2 = 3 hours. (Not 9 hours: 11 − 2 = 9 does not work across noon.)

items.q: Put these times in order from earliest to latest in one day: 3:00 p.m., 7:00 a.m., 9:30 p.m., 11:00 a.m.
items.e: All a.m. times come first, then the p.m. times. a.m.: 7:00, then 11:00. p.m.: 3:00, then 9:30. So the order is 7:00 a.m., 11:00 a.m., 3:00 p.m., 9:30 p.m.

items.q: A digital clock shows 4:37 p.m. How many minutes is it until 5:00 p.m.?
items.e: An hour has 60 minutes. It is 37 minutes past 4. 60 − 37 = 23 minutes until 5:00 p.m. (Not 63: that uses 100 − 37, but an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: What day of the week is September 1, 2027?
items.e: Find the 1 on the calendar. Look up its column to the day name: Wednesday. (Not Sunday: the month does not always start in the first column.)

items.q: Today is Monday, October 4. What is the date 1 week from today?
items.e: 1 week is 7 days. 4 + 7 = 11, so it is Monday, October 11. (October 14 counts a week as 10 days.)

items.q: Today is Wednesday. What day will it be in 3 days?
items.e: Count 3 jumps: Wednesday → Thursday → Friday → Saturday. (Friday counts today as one of the days.)

items.q: The green box is Chloe’s first day of school. What day of the week is it?
items.e: The box is around the 7. Look up the column: it is a Tuesday. So the first day of school is Tuesday, September 7.

items.q: Which month has 30 days?
items.e: April, June, September and November have 30 days. March, July and August have 31 days. So the answer is April.

items.q: Mateo’s school has its Terry Fox Run on the circled day. What is the date?
items.e: The red circle is around the 23. Look up the column: it is a Thursday. So the date is Thursday, September 23.

items.q: How many days are in February 2027?
items.e: February is the shortest month. In 2027 it has 28 days. (It has 29 days only in a leap year, such as 2028.)

items.q: How many Wednesdays are in September 2027?
items.e: Look down the Wed column: 1, 8, 15, 22, 29. That is 5 Wednesdays. (Many months have 4, but count to be sure.)

items.q: Ava’s birthday is on the last day of June. What is the date?
items.e: June has 30 days, so the last day of June is June 30. (There is no June 31. July 1 is Canada Day, the next day.)

items.q: Canada Day is July 1. What day of the week is Canada Day in 2027?
items.e: Find the 1 and look up its column: Thursday. (Not Sunday: the first column is not always the 1st.)

items.q: Which month comes 3 months after November?
items.e: Count 3 jumps: November → December → January → February. (January counts November as one of the months.)

items.q: BC Day is a holiday on the first Monday in August. What is the date of BC Day in 2027?
items.e: Look down the Mon column. The first Monday is the 2nd. So BC Day is Monday, August 2. (August 1 is a Sunday. August 9 is the second Monday.)

items.q: How many days is it from the first day of school to the Terry Fox Run?
items.e: Count the jumps from 7 to 23: 23 − 7 = 16 days. That is 2 weeks (to the 21st) and 2 more days. (17 counts the first day too. 23 is just the date.)

items.q: Zara’s Spring Break starts on Monday, March 15. It is 2 weeks long. On what date does she go back to school?
items.e: Each row of the calendar is 1 week. Go down 2 rows from the 15: 15 + 7 + 7 = 29. School starts again on Monday, March 29. (March 22 is only 1 week later. March 25 counts a week as 5 days.)

items.q: June has 30 days. How many weeks and days is that?
items.e: 4 weeks = 4 × 7 = 28 days. 30 − 28 = 2 days left. So 30 days = 4 weeks 2 days. (3 weeks counts a week as 10 days.)

items.q: Thanksgiving is Monday, October 11. Halloween is October 31. How many days is it from Thanksgiving to Halloween?
items.e: Count the jumps from 11 to 31: 31 − 11 = 20 days. (21 counts Thanksgiving too.)

items.q: Kai has a soccer game every Saturday. The first game is May 1. What is the date of the third game?
items.e: The games are 1 week apart. First game: May 1. Second: May 8. Third: May 15. (May 22 adds 3 weeks to the first game, but that is the fourth game.)

items.q: Jasleen borrows a library book on Wednesday, October 6. It is due in 3 weeks. What is the due date?
items.e: 3 weeks = 7 + 7 + 7 = 21 days. 6 + 21 = 27. The book is due on Wednesday, October 27. (October 9 adds 3 days, not 3 weeks. October 20 is only 2 weeks.)

items.q: Nadia’s family goes camping in the Okanagan. They arrive on Friday, July 9 and go home on Monday, July 12. How many nights do they sleep in the tent?
items.e: Count the jumps: Friday night, Saturday night and Sunday night. 12 − 9 = 3 nights. (4 counts the days Friday, Saturday, Sunday and Monday.)

items.q: Which is the longest time?
items.e: 1 year = 12 months = about 52 weeks = 365 days. 11 months, 50 weeks and 300 days are all a bit less. So the longest is 1 year.
Both times are in the same hour. 30 − 15 = 15 minutes.

items.q: Gym class starts at 1:05 p.m. and ends at 1:45 p.m. How long is gym class?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 45 − 5 = 40 minutes.
Both times are in the same hour. 35 − 10 = 25 minutes.

items.q: Liam starts the Terry Fox Run at 1:15 p.m. He finishes at 1:52 p.m. How long does he take?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 52 − 15 = 37 minutes.
The minutes are the same, so count the hours. Count the jumps, not the numbers: 9:00 a.m. → 10:00 a.m. That is 1 hour. (1 hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Harjot’s family hikes in Stanley Park from 1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. How long is the hike?
items.e: The minutes are the same, so count the hours. Count the jumps, not the numbers: 1:00 p.m. → 2:00 p.m. → 3:00 p.m. That is 2 hours. (1 hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Recess starts at 10:15 a.m. It lasts 15 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Count on 15 minutes from 10:15: 15 + 15 = 30. It is still the morning, so recess ends at 10:30 a.m. (11:15 a.m. would be 1 hour later.)

items.q: The bus for the field trip to Science World leaves at 9:35 a.m. It gets there at 10:20 a.m. How long is the bus ride?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 9:35 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 25 minutes. Then 10:00 a.m. to 10:20 a.m. is 20 minutes. 25 + 20 = 45 minutes. (Not 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Ryan rides the SkyTrain from 3:45 p.m. to 4:10 p.m. How long is the ride?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 3:45 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 15 minutes. Then 4:00 p.m. to 4:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 15 + 10 = 25 minutes. (Not 65 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Ji-woo’s swimming lesson is from 4:45 p.m. to 5:20 p.m. How long is it?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 4:45 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 15 minutes. Then 5:00 p.m. to 5:20 p.m. is 20 minutes. 15 + 20 = 35 minutes. (Not 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Wei goes to bed at 8:30 p.m. He reads for 20 minutes before bed. What time does he start reading?
items.e: Count back 20 minutes from 8:30: 30 − 20 = 10. Reading starts at 8:10 p.m. (8:50 p.m. is 20 minutes after bedtime.)

items.q: Art starts at 1:40 p.m. It lasts 50 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: From 1:40 p.m., 20 minutes takes you to 2:00 p.m. 50 − 20 = 30 more minutes makes 2:30 p.m. (2:40 p.m. would be 1 hour later, not 50 minutes.)

items.q: A hockey game starts at 6:30 p.m. and ends at 8:00 p.m. How long is the game?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 6:30 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 30 minutes. Then 7:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. is 1 hour. 30 + 60 = 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes.

items.q: A BC Ferries boat leaves Tsawwassen at 11:00 a.m. It gets to Swartz Bay on Vancouver Island at 12:35 p.m. How long is the trip?
items.e: From 11:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 1 hour. Then 12:00 noon to 12:35 p.m. is 35 minutes. So it is 1 hour 35 minutes.

items.q: Owen’s lacrosse practice is from 5:30 p.m. to 6:50 p.m. How long is practice?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 5:30 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. is 30 minutes. Then 6:00 p.m. to 6:50 p.m. is 50 minutes. 30 + 50 = 80 minutes = 1 hour 20 minutes.

items.q: Noah’s soccer game starts at 6:10 p.m. He leaves home 25 minutes before the game. What time does he leave home?
items.e: Count back 10 minutes to 6:00 p.m. 25 − 10 = 15, so count back 15 more minutes: 5:45 p.m. (6:35 p.m. is 25 minutes after 6:10. 5:35 p.m. is 35 minutes before.)

items.q: A BC Ferries boat leaves at 9:20 a.m. The trip takes 1 hour 35 minutes. What time does the boat arrive?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 9:20 a.m. → 10:20 a.m. Then add 35 minutes: 20 + 35 = 55. The boat arrives at 10:55 a.m. (9:55 a.m. forgets the 1 hour.)

items.q: School starts at 8:45 a.m. and ends at 3:00 p.m. How long is the school day?
items.e: 8:45 a.m. to 2:45 p.m. is 6 hours. 2:45 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 15 more minutes. So the school day is 6 hours 15 minutes. (Not 7 hours 15 minutes: 8:45 a.m. to 3:45 p.m. would be 7 hours, and school ends before 3:45.)

items.q: Mei’s dad puts salmon in the oven at 5:50 p.m. It bakes for 25 minutes. What time is it ready?
items.e: From 5:50 p.m., 10 minutes takes you to 6:00 p.m. 25 − 10 = 15 more minutes makes 6:15 p.m. (6:25 p.m. adds 25 minutes to 6:00 instead of to 5:50.)

items.q: Simran’s movie is 1 hour 30 minutes long. Arjun’s movie is 95 minutes long. Whose movie is longer, and by how much?
items.e: 1 hour 30 minutes = 60 + 30 = 90 minutes. 95 − 90 = 5. So Arjun’s movie is longer, by 5 minutes. (Not Simran’s by 35: that counts an hour as 100 minutes.)
